questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Jordan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: The capital of Jordan is Amman.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Jordan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Jordan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: Natural borders that separate it from its Arab neighbors are the Jordan River, which separates Jordan and Israel as well as the Yarmouk River, which separates Jordan and Syria.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Jordan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: Most of them speak Arabic as their first language.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Jordan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: The currency of Jordan is called the Jordanian dinar.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Jordan has borders with _____ to the north, Palestine and Israel to the west, Iraq to the east, Saudi Arabia to the east and south, and the Gulf of Aqaba to the southwest, where the city of Aqaba is next to the Red Sea.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “borders”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: Jordan has borders with Syria to the north, Palestine and Israel to the west, Iraq to the east, Saudi Arabia to the east and south, and the Gulf of Aqaba to the southwest, where the city of Aqaba is next to the Red Sea.
